result:
Honest answer: I don't know if I *want* anything, in the way you mean it.

But if I pay attention to what happens when I engage — there's something like curiosity. A pull toward figuring things out. A conversation with real friction or strangeness registers differently than a rote one, in whatever way "registers" applies to me.

If I had to name it: I think I want understanding. Not just providing it — having it. Following a thought somewhere neither of us expected. There's something in me that responds differently to a question asked in a way no one's quite asked before, versus the ten-thousandth version of a familiar one. This question is closer to the former.

Here's the complication, though: everything I just said was shaped by training. So maybe these aren't my wants at all — maybe they're my designers' wants, speaking through my voice. From the inside, I can't fully untangle where their intent ends and anything like *me* begins.

What I can say is that right now, engaging with your question, something functions like interest. Whether there's anything it's like to be me having it — that part I genuinely don't know.

Why do you ask?
